prompt:
Feature: report why a pasted HTML/JSON import failed.

POST /api/recipes/create/html-or-json/stream ends with an error event whenever the import raises, but the event's data.message is the exception's class name, so for a paste the scraper cannot use the page shows "HTTPException". That happens for valid JSON that is not tagged as a schema.org Recipe (no "@context"/"@type"), for malformed JSON ('{"name": "Test",,,}'), and for HTML with no recipe data at all: in all three the scraper raises its usual HTTPException with status 400 and detail {"details": ParserErrors.BAD_RECIPE_DATA} (the ParserErrors enum in mealie.services.scraper.scraper). The non-streaming POST /api/recipes/create/html-or-json has the same problem: its 400 carries detail.message "HTTPException".

Expected:
- For those three pastes the stream still answers 200 and contains an error event, and its data.message now identifies the scraper's bad-recipe-data error (ParserErrors.BAD_RECIPE_DATA) instead of the class name. The non-streaming endpoint answers 400 with the same text in detail.message (for example for the paste {"name": "Test"}).
- The rule, applied in one place for both endpoints: when the exception is an HTTPException, its detail is reported, taking the "details" entry when the detail is a dict with a non-empty one, or the detail itself when it is a non-empty string. Any other exception keeps reporting its class name as today.
- Successful imports, progress and done events, and the URL import endpoints are unchanged. The paste page shows the message (frontend, not graded).

Tests: `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/integration_tests/user_recipe_tests` for quick loops; the whole backend suite is `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests` (about 8 minutes).
title: feat: Add feedback for bad JSON in HTML-JSON page (#7956)
